method: sweep.py scenarios --family <redstone family> (tools/bds-sweep/circuits.py): each circuit is built in a cell of its own with block updates (`build`), left `wait` ticks, then run for a `timeline` of N server ticks in which `events` ([tick, event]) are applied at their tick and every `watch` offset is read once per tick after them. `trace` lists [tick, watch index, block, states] for the first read and every change. `witness` is the tick (2 or 3) at which a dust beside a redstone block set at tick 0 outside the cells lit in the same wave: BDS works redstone every other tick, and an update shows at the reads whose tick has the parity of `witness`. Offsets are relative to the cell origin on the superflat grass (the floor is y=-1); `minecraft:` is left out of block names.
